status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 the IRA half of this objective is largely enacted through reconciliation, while the IIJA half has not been repealed and Congress chose not to rescind unobligated IIJA funds in FY2026 appropriations. Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) ended or restricted many IRA credits: the U.S. Code text shows the residential clean energy credit (26 U.S.C. 25D) applies only to expenditures made through 2025-12-31 (section 70506), the clean vehicle credit (30D) only to vehicles acquired through 2025-09-30 (section 70502), the clean hydrogen credit (45V) only to facilities whose construction begins before 2028-01-01 (section 70511), and the wind and solar credit (45Y) not to wind or solar facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 (section 70512, applying to facilities whose construction begins more than 12 months after enactment). The law also repealed the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund (42 U.S.C. 7434, section 60002), and a law-firm summary reports it rescinded unobligated IRA loan funding while creating an Energy Dominance Financing program. Executive Order 14154 (2025-01-20) paused IRA and IIJA disbursements, and DOE announced on 2025-10-01 the termination of 321 awards supporting 223 projects, estimated at about 7.56 billion dollars in savings, after a case-by-case financial review. Courts have since ordered reinstatement of 27.6 million dollars in commitments (January 2026) and vacated 11 grant cancellations worth 82.1 million dollars (2026-06-11), and 13 states sued over hydrogen hub cancellations (2026-02-18). The FY2026 Energy and Water act (Division B of Public Law 119-74, approved 2026-01-23) gave the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations no appropriation and, per Holland & Knight, reprogrammed about 5.16 billion dollars in unobligated IIJA funds rather than rescinding them.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 orders agencies to pause disbursement of IRA and IIJA funds pending review, with release subject to review and approval by OMB and the economic policy adviser.

Public Law 119-21 is signed. Per the U.S. Code text as amended: the residential clean energy credit ends for expenditures after 2025-12-31 (section 70506), the clean vehicle credit for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30 (section 70502), and the clean hydrogen credit requires construction to begin before 2028-01-01 (section 70511); wind and solar facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 lose the section 45Y credit (section 70512); the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund statute is repealed (section 60002). The law's table of contents also lists rescissions of other IRA funds (Sec. 50402 and Secs. 60003 to 60024) and Energy Dominance Financing (Sec. 50403), which were not read.
timeline.source: U.S. Code via Cornell Legal Information Institute

timeline.event: A law-firm alert summarizes credit end dates in the enacted law: residential clean energy and home improvement credits 2025-12-31, clean vehicle credits 2025-09-30, clean hydrogen construction start by 2027-12-31, and wind and solar unavailable for construction starting on or after 2026-07-04 when placed in service after 2027-12-31; it lists no termination change for the carbon sequestration and nuclear credits. The alert notes a conflict between its chart and text on the phase-out of other technologies.

A law-firm alert reports that all unobligated Loan Programs Office funding appropriated through the IRA was rescinded, and that a new Energy Dominance Financing program received a 1 billion dollar credit subsidy appropriation available through 2028-09-30.

IRS Notice 2025-42 on beginning-of-construction rules for wind and solar takes effect for construction starting on or after this date; it states the credits end for facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 unless construction began before 2026-07-05 (the notice's issuance date is not shown on the page).

DOE announces it has terminated 321 financial awards supporting 223 projects, with estimated savings of about 7.56 billion dollars, issued by OCED, EERE, GDO, MESC, ARPA-E and Fossil Energy; DOE says a case-by-case financial review found the projects did not adequately serve energy needs or return enough value, notes that 26 percent of the terminated awards were made between Election Day and Inauguration Day, and gives recipients 30 days to appeal. S&P Global reports the two largest awards, 2.2 billion dollars, were for West Coast hydrogen hubs.

The FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations act, Division B of Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938, approved 2026-01-23 per govinfo), is enacted; its text was not readable. The Business Council for Sustainable Energy reports it funds the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations at zero, and Holland & Knight reports it contains no rescissions and reprograms about 5.164 billion dollars of unobligated IIJA funds, letting Congress carry the balances over.

California, Washington and other states sue DOE in the Northern District of California over the October 2025 cancellations of hydrogen hub and other awards, arguing the cuts violate separation of powers and that a May 2025 DOE review memorandum is a pretext.

A federal judge in the District of Columbia vacates DOE's cancellation of 11 EERE grants worth 82.1 million dollars (date inferred from an article published 2026-06-12); a January 2026 ruling in a similar case had ordered DOE to reinstate 27.6 million dollars in commitments on equal protection grounds.

title: Repeal IIJA and IRA energy programs and rescind unspent funds
uncertainties: The text of Public Law 119-21 was not read directly (govinfo's page stops partway through the first title); the credit end dates were verified against the amended sections of the U.S. Code at Cornell's Legal Information Institute through fetch summaries, which cover sections 25D, 30D, 45V, 45Y and the repealed 42 U.S.C. 7434 but not section 25C or the carbon sequestration and nuclear credits (the Pierce Atwood alert is the source for the home improvement credit ending 2025-12-31 and for no termination change on those two). The wind and solar rule is a placed-in-service cutoff of 2027-12-31 for facilities whose construction begins after 2026-07-04; facilities that begin construction earlier keep the earlier rules, and IRS Notice 2025-42 addresses beginning of construction. The Energy Dominance Financing and IRA loan rescission claims rest on a law-firm alert and the law's table of contents. DOE's 2025-10-01 release was read through a fetch summary; the 13-state suit and the 27.6 million dollar January 2026 outcome rest on S&P Global, and the 2026-06-11 ruling (Judge Mehta, D.D.C., a suit led by the American Institute of Chemical Engineers on equal protection grounds, per Utility Dive) has no caption or docket number and its date is inferred from an article published 2026-06-12. Utility Dive's description of the January outcome (a settlement versus an order) is inconsistent. The text of Division B of Public Law 119-74 could not be read, so the FY2026 reprogramming of unobligated IIJA funds rests on Holland & Knight (written before signing); the two sources conflict on Grid Deployment Office funding, so none is used. Litigation over the January 2025 funding pause (Executive Order 14154) was not researched.
